title: Attempt ledger — the record that makes 'one attempt' mean anything
description:
An append-only, hash-linked record of every assessment served to one person. It carries two loads: the no-retake rule for challenge exams (decision 31), and exposure control, since it is the only place that knows which archetypes a candidate has already met.

THE HONEST LIMIT, STATED UP FRONT. In the Personal edition the ledger lives on the candidate's own machine and is signed with the candidate's own key. Hash-linking makes edits to the MIDDLE of the chain detectable, but nothing local can stop a holder truncating the tail and continuing from an earlier point — they hold every key involved. The chain is therefore trustworthy only as far as its most recent EXTERNAL anchor: a head countersigned by someone who is not the holder. Every signoff produces one, because there is no self-signoff anywhere in this system, so any credential above self-study carries an anchor with it. An unanchored ledger supports self-study claims and nothing more, which is exactly what the self-study provenance tier already means. This is not a weakness patched over; it is the reason the provenance tiers exist.

subject.description: Whose ledger this is. One ledger per person, never per organization: the record has to follow the person between employers or the no-retake rule resets every time they change jobs.

entries.description: Ordered, append-only, hash-linked. Index 0 has prevHash null; every later entry chains to the one before it.

anchors.description: External attestations of a chain head. Each one fixes history up to that point: anything at or before an anchored head cannot be rewritten without invalidating an attestation somebody else signed. Produced naturally at every signoff, and optionally by publishing a head to a Commons instance.

attestedBy.description: MUST NOT be the ledger's own subject. A holder attesting their own history anchors nothing, and the validator rejects it.

context.description: Why this anchor exists. `organization-custody` covers the dual-custody copy an ISO/IEC 17025 laboratory holds for audit, which anchors the chain as a side effect of a record-keeping obligation the laboratory already has.

sequence.description: Position in the chain, strictly increasing by one. Redundant with array order and checked against it — a ledger whose sequence and order disagree has been edited.

mode.description: `practice` is unlimited and carries no consequence — learning must not be rationed. `assessment` is the ordinary route and may be reattempted subject to waiting periods. `challenge-exam` is ONE attempt per element and level, ever, with no retake: it lets an experienced hire skip content without pretending they need it, and that offer is only credible if it cannot be farmed.

archetype.description: Which shape was served. This is what makes the ledger the exposure-control record as well as the attempt record.

exposureGroup.description: Copied from the binding. Bindings sharing a group count as one exposure, so near-identical items drawn from one archetype across adjacent elements cannot be served repeatedly.

drawHash.description: Hash of the exact parameter draw served. Lets an item be reconstructed years later when a credential is re-reviewed, and proves two candidates did not receive the same numbers.

outcome.description: `abandoned` counts as an attempt for challenge-exam purposes — otherwise a candidate reads the paper, walks away, and returns prepared. `voided` does not, and exists for a defective item or a platform fault; voiding requires a reason and is the only outcome an organization can apply retrospectively.

voidReason.description: Required when outcome is `voided`. A void with no stated reason is indistinguishable from a quietly erased failure.

prevHash.description: Hash of the previous entry; null only at sequence 0.

hash.description: Hash over this entry's content together with prevHash. Recomputed on verification; a mismatch anywhere invalidates everything after it.
